title: Do Not Take the Last Stone
problem: Fifteen stones are on a table. Players alternately remove 1, 2, or 3 stones, but the player who removes the last stone loses. Can the first player force a win, and how?

hints.text: Work backward carefully because a pile of one is losing for the player to move.

solution.setup: Backward induction shows positions congruent to 1 modulo 4 are losing.
solution.reasoning: From 1 a player must take the last stone and lose. From 2,3,4 a player can leave 1. From 5 every move leaves 2,3,or4, so 5 is losing; the pattern repeats every four. Since 15≡3 mod4, remove 2 to leave 13, then make each pair of removals total 4. Eventually the opponent receives one stone and must take it.
solution.finalAnswer: Yes. Remove 2 first, then complement the opponent's moves to 4.
solution.sanityCheck: The strategy leaves 13,9,5,1 after the first player's turns, all losing states for the opponent.

keyInsight: Changing the terminal rule shifts the modular losing states from multiples of four to numbers congruent to one.
recognitionCues: A normal take-away game with a reversed last-move condition requires recomputing base cases before extending a pattern.
commonMistakes: Using the ordinary-play strategy and treating 0 as the only losing state.
followUps: Generalize the losing states when players may remove 1 through m stones.
